title: Make each tracking-plan item's identity mirror its path

facts.note: The resolved root is topology.telemetry_root in atdd-bun.yaml when set. Otherwise it is the default `telemetry/`. The default root does not activate when a different root is configured. All JSON files under the resolved root are in scope, whether new, changed or unchanged.
Every .json file under the resolved root is judged as a tracking-plan item.
Adoption gate. A new observer must detect that a telemetry root exists or that some acceptance declares telemetry. Without adoption the rule emits nothing.
Planner tasks that add, change or review observations.

fires: A planner adds <root>/<theme>/<artifact>/event.<plane>.json for a new observable outcome
A tracking-plan file is renamed or moved, and its id or logical_artifact no longer matches the new path
An existing, unchanged tracking-plan item in an adopted repository has an id that does not match its path
A metric item file has no measure segment, or an event, trace or log file has one
The repository configures topology.telemetry_root, and a JSON item under that configured root is checked
doesNotFire: The repository has no telemetry root and no acceptance declares telemetry (it has not opted in)
JSON files outside the resolved telemetry root, including files under `telemetry/` when a different topology.telemetry_root is configured
Non-JSON files under the telemetry root

given: Telemetry is adopted, and a JSON file exists under the telemetry root. The root is `telemetry/` by default. If topology.telemetry_root is set in atdd-bun.yaml, that path replaces the default. The file may be new, changed or unchanged.
when: You plan, author, rename or review a tracking-plan item at <root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>].json
then: Make the item's declared identity mirror its path: id = telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}], logical_artifact = telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, and the file name's kind, plane and measure equal the declared fields.
prefer: Name the file for what it is, then derive id and logical_artifact from the path.

Keep the file valid against telemetry-plan.schema.json. Declare id, a SemVer version, logical_artifact, kind, plane, owner, purpose, acceptances, properties and required. Optionally add forbidden_properties. Give each property a type, classification and cardinality. Every `required` name must be declared in `properties`. Metric dimensions are optional, but each one present must declare cardinality.
Give every metric item a measure segment (metric.<plane>.<measure>.json, id ending :{measure}). Never give an event, trace or log item a measure segment.
avoid: Renaming a file or hand-editing an id so that the path and the identity drift apart
Declaring the same concrete id in two files
Putting notes, indexes or generated bundles under the telemetry root
Treating a logical artifact as an exporter event
unless: Telemetry is not adopted: there is no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration. Adoption means creating the tree or making the first acceptance decision.
why: The telemetry tree is a registry, not a suggestion. The path is the authority for identity, so a renamed file or a hand-edited id cannot drift apart silently.
evidence: Every .json file under the resolved telemetry root validates against telemetry-plan.schema.json.

For each file, the kind, plane and measure parsed from the file name match the declared fields. The id equals telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}] and the logical_artifact equals telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, both derived from the path.
No concrete id is declared by more than one file.
With no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration, the validator emits no findings.
In an adopted repository, an unchanged item that is invalid is still reported. Checks cover all items, not only changed ones.
Every metric item has a measure segment in its file name and id. No event, trace or log item has one.
verifier_detail: Telemetry root: `telemetry/` by default, configurable as topology.telemetry_root in atdd-bun.yaml. It is the versioned tracking-plan source of truth.
Path grammar: <root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>].json. Metric items carry a measure segment. Event, trace and log items never do.

Local shape is the JSON Schema's job (telemetry-plan.schema.json): required identity fields, URN grammar, SemVer core version, property declarations with classification and cardinality, and metric dimensions that declare cardinality.

This rule covers the cross-artifact checks that the Schema cannot see. (1) The file name's kind, plane and measure match the declared fields. (2) The id equals telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}] derived from the path. (3) The logical_artifact equals telemetry:{theme}:{artifact} from the path. (4) The names in `required` are a subset of the `properties` keys. (5) No two files declare the same concrete id.
Item fields: id, version, logical_artifact, kind, plane, owner, purpose, acceptances, properties, required. Optional: forbidden_properties and, for metrics only, dimensions.

Concrete item: a telemetry URN with kind and plane, telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}]. Logical artifact: the stable architectural identity of an observable outcome, telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}. A logical artifact is not an exporter event; the concrete items under it are.
Every .json file under the root is judged as an item. Non-item JSON has no allow-list.
Adoption gate: with no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration anywhere, emit nothing. Upgrading the package must not fail a repository that has not opted in.

Reference fix example (source fix_hint), the file telemetry/commons/response-invocation-accepted/event.be.json: {"id": "telemetry:event:be:commons:response-invocation-accepted", "version": "1.0.0", "logical_artifact": "telemetry:commons:response-invocation-accepted", "kind": "event", "plane": "be", "owner": "commons", "purpose": "Records that a response invocation passed acceptance so ingress health can be audited.", "acceptances": ["acc:commons:E001-UNIT-001"], "properties": { "response_id": { "type": "string", "classification": "internal", "cardinality": "high" } }, "required": ["response_id"], "forbidden_properties": ["raw_payload", "secret", "prompt"]}

Scope resolution: scan only the resolved root. When topology.telemetry_root is set, it replaces `telemetry/` and does not add to it. After adoption, scan all JSON files under the root regardless of diff status.
audit: Original name: Tracking-plan items are versioned, path-mirrored registry entries

splitSuggestion.then: Each tracking-plan item validates against telemetry-plan.schema.json: required fields, URN grammar, SemVer version, properties with classification and cardinality, and metric dimensions with cardinality when present.
Every name in an item's `required` is declared in its `properties`.
No two tracking-plan files declare the same concrete telemetry id.
Only tracking-plan items live under the telemetry root.

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: `then` keeps the single obligation that identity mirrors the path. Schema validity, required⊆properties, concrete-id uniqueness and root-holds-only-items are independently testable. They are kept here as prefer/avoid/evidence/verifier_detail and are proposed as separate conventions in splitSuggestion.
additions.justification: The one-obligation-in-then rule. The source bundles all of them in one REQUIRED statement.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires and doesNotFire were derived from the statement, the exceptions and the telemetry_root term. Scope is the resolved root, and all items are in scope after adoption.
additions.justification: The schema requires explicit activation. No new obligation is added.

additions.text: Unchanged invalid items in an adopted repository are still reported.
additions.justification: Makes explicit the source's 'every JSON file under the telemetry root' scope. It is not a new obligation.
